news.title: History Under the Lights! 48th One Day Encounter Goes Day-Night at SSC
news.summary: A rivalry of legends. A bond of brothers. And now, a historic first. For the first time in the history of the series dating back to 1924, the Maroon flag flies high under the lights at SSC for the Day-Night One Day encounter.
news.content:
A rivalry of legends. A bond of brothers. And now, a historic first in the storied annals of Sri Lankan school cricket.

The Battle of the Maroons Joint Organising Committee announced that the 48th One Day Encounter between Ananda College and Nalanda College will be played under lights as a Day-Night encounter at the prestigious Sinhalese Sports Club (SSC) grounds in Colombo.

Speaking at the announcement, Co-Chairs Mahela Jayawardena and Upali Dharmadasa stated that this innovation brings an electrifying modern spectacle to one of the most cherished sporting traditions in South Asia, enabling thousands of working alumni, families, and young cricketers to experience the vibrant festival atmosphere after dusk.

Both teams will compete in coloured clothing with a white ball under international-standard broadcast floodlights, marking a revolutionary milestone for the P. De S. Kularatne Memorial Trophy.
news.author: Varuna Ratnaweera

news.title: Battle of the Maroons 96th Edition Launched at Cinnamon Grand Gala
news.summary: The Joint Organising Committee organized a colourful gala at the Cinnamon Grand Hotel to honour sponsors of the 95th encounter, present Rs 25 million to the colleges, and unveil plans for the 96th edition.
news.content:
The Battle of the Maroons Joint Organising Committee organised a colourful function at the Cinnamon Grand Hotel on 20th November to pay tribute to the sponsoring companies of the 95th Battle of the Maroons and to officially launch the 96th Battle of the Maroons scheduled at the SSC grounds.

Sri Lanka Cricketing Legend Mahela Jayawardena, who Co-Chairs the BoM Organising Committee with Upali Dharmadasa, welcomed the participants and paid a glowing tribute to the partnering companies who made it possible for the organisers to achieve their ambitious development targets.

A generous contribution of Rs 25 million from the proceeds of the 95th big match was presented directly to the two Principals, Mr. Lal Dissanayake (Ananda College) and Mr. Iran Champika Silva (Nalanda College), to support grassroots cricket facilities and student welfare.

The ceremonial first ticket of the 96th Battle of the Maroons was presented to two of Sri Lanka's most esteemed cricketing legends from Ananda and Nalanda, Brendon Kuruppu and Hemantha Devapriya.
news.author: Varuna Ratnaweera

news.title: Public Notice: Unauthorised Flight Package and Booking Advisory
news.summary: Joint Committee clarifies that circulating social media flight promotions from Melbourne are not endorsed or approved by either school or the committee.
news.content:
It has come to the attention of the Joint Organising Committee that social media advertisements have been circulating promoting a 'Battle of the Maroons: Special Group Flight Package' from Melbourne to Colombo.

We wish to clarify that this promotion is NOT organized, endorsed, or approved by the official Battle of the Maroons Joint Organising Committee or by the administrations of Ananda College or Nalanda College.

We kindly urge all old boys, families, and supporters not to consider this as an official offer and to exercise extreme caution before committing funds or personal details.

All verified information, including official travel arrangements and ticket sales, is communicated exclusively through our verified web portal at battleofthemaroons.lk and recognized alumni association channels.
news.author: Varuna Ratnaweera

news.title: Maroons Arrived in 6 Charter Flights from London & Melbourne for Big Match
news.summary: Hundreds of overseas alumni flew back on special SriLankan Airlines charter flights flown and coordinated entirely by Anandian and Nalandian pilots and air traffic controllers.
news.content:
Many Anandians and Nalandians based overseas make it a sacred point to return to Sri Lanka during March every year to cherish the camaraderie of the Big Match.

For the first time in the history of the Ananda–Nalanda Big Match, the Organising Committee partnered with national carrier SriLankan Airlines to arrange preferential reservations and dedicated flights from Melbourne and London.

In an extraordinary display of heritage, the pilots who captained the aircraft, the senior flight attendants, and the air traffic controllers who guided the planes safely into Bandaranaike International Airport were all proud alumni of Ananda and Nalanda Colleges.

Passengers burst into spirited school anthems as the flights touched down in Colombo, kicking off a week of unforgettable festivities.
news.author: Varuna Ratnaweera

news.title: Historic Inaugural 3-Day Game Ends in High-Scoring Draw at SSC
news.summary: 95th Battle of the Maroons witnessed majestic centuries from Dinada Athalage (131) and Nadul Jayalath (111) in front of Sidath Wettimuni and Roshan Mahanama.
news.content:
Many expected a decisive result in the 95th Battle of the Maroons, which for the first time in the encounter's history dating back to 1924, was staged across three days.

With an opening ceremony graced by Mr. Sidath Wettimuni and Mr. Roshan Mahanama, spectators were treated to batsmanship of the highest pedigree. Dinada Athalage steered Ananda to 324/6 declared with an exquisite 131 in 287 balls, while Nadul Jayalath anchored Nalanda with a gritty 111 in 192 deliveries to reach 325/6 declared.

Sharada Jayarathne captured 4 for 58 for Ananda. Brief weather interruptions on days two and three ultimately led to a sporting draw, with both sets of players receiving ovations from packed stands.
news.author: Varuna Ratnaweera

news.title: Parade of the Maroons & Friction Musical Extravaganza Rocks Colombo
news.summary: A massive vehicle procession of decorated vintage cars, trucks, and floats traversed the streets of Colombo, culminating in the annual Friction musical festival.
news.content:
The annual Parade of the Maroons brought the streets of Colombo to a celebratory standstill as thousands of students, past cricketers, and distinguished old boys joined a colourful motorcade spanning several kilometers.

Flags of maroon, gold, and silver fluttered from sports cars and open-top lorries equipped with brass and papare ensembles. The procession culminated at the grounds for the Friction Musical Show, headlined by top Sri Lankan artists, celebrating the unbroken fellowship between both colleges.
news.author: Varuna Ratnaweera

featuredMatches.summary: Two stalwarts of Maroons cricket, Mr. Saliya Senanayake and Mr. Palitha Seneviratne (captains in the 1970s), graced the opening. Ananda posted 249/9 in 50 overs with Kenul de Zoysa scoring 39. Nalanda were 62/2 in 12.2 overs when torrential rain stopped play. As minimum 20 overs required for D/L method could not be completed, the match was declared a no-decision and the trophy was shared.
